observations.source_title: FPL Wood Handbook, GTR-190 (2010), Chapter 5, Table 5-5a
observations.basis_verbatim: Table 5-5a's own footnote a says only: "Results of tests on clear, straight-grained specimens. Property values were taken from world literature ... Some property values have been adjusted to 12% moisture content." It does not say whether Specific gravity is ovendry weight over green volume or over 12%-MC volume (contrast Table 5-3a footnote b and Table 5-4a footnote a, both quoted in the stored excerpt, which do state that basis for their own SG columns). Resolved by FPL Ch.4 (source_id g7_fpl_gtr190_ch4_sg_conversion, sources/fpl_gtr190_ch4_sg_conversion_excerpt.txt): "Some specific gravity data are reported in Tables 5-3, 5-4, and 5-5 (Chap. 5) on both the green (basic) and 12% MC volume basis." Table 4-5 defines Gb (basic specific gravity) as ovendry mass / green volume. So this row's printed SG, on the table's 'Green' line, is Gb.
observations.derivation: FPL Ch.4 Eq. (4-11): Gx = Gb / [1 - 0.265 Gb (1 - x/MCfs)], x = 12, MCfs = 30 (FPL's stated average fiber saturation point; no species-specific MCfs is printed for RadiataPine), so a = (30-12)/30 = 0.6 and Gx = Gb / (1 - 0.159 Gb). Gb = 0.42 -> gm12 = 0.45005. rho12 = gm12 x 1000 x 1.12 (Table 5-3a-style basis: mass at 12% MC over volume at 12% MC) = 504.06 kg/m3. Eq. (4-11) itself is verified against FPL's own worked white-ash example in the Ch.4 excerpt (0.4% agreement).
observations.notes: FPL does have a Table 5-5a row for Radiata pine, so the plan's fallback list (Scion, NZ Wood, CSIRO, Wood Database) is not needed to fill a missing row. See the second row below (source g7_wood_database_radiata_pine, grade c) for a cross-check that resolves the basis question with a printed 12%-MC-basis SG. Updated 2026-09-25: FPL Ch.4 Eq. (4-11) now gives an FPL-only rho12 of 504.06 kg/m3 for this row (ratio to the Wood Database cross-check: 0.9884).

observations.basis_verbatim: "The first number is the basic specific gravity, based on the botanical standard of ovendry weight and green volume. The second number is meant for woodworkers, and is simply a snapshot of the wood's specific gravity at 12% MC, (that is, both 12% MC weight and volume)."
observations.derivation: rho12 = SG_12%MC x 1000 = 0.51 x 1000 = 510 kg/m3. No x1.12 ovendry-to-wet-mass factor here: unlike the FPL Table 5-3a convention (SG basis = ovendry mass / volume-at-12%-MC, needing the x1.12 step to reach a wet-mass-at-12%-MC density), this source's second SG number already has both mass and volume at 12% MC, so multiplying by the density of water (1000 kg/m3) gives rho12 directly. Cross-check: the source's own printed 'Average Dried Weight: 32 lbs/ft3 (515 kg/m3)' is 515 kg/m3, close to the 510 kg/m3 computed here (the site's own kg/m3 conversion of the lbs/ft3 figure rounds differently; both are the same SG to two figures).
observations.notes: Aggregator, not a primary source; used only because FPL Table 5-5a's own footnote does not state the SG basis for its Radiata pine row (see the row above). Not the plan's grade-c fallback for a missing FPL row (FPL does have a row) -- it is a secondary cross-check per the task's item 3.
